newsitem.title: USA: Conf Bd sees holiday lifting retail sales 5.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Conf Bd sees holiday lifting retail sales 5.5 pct.

text.p: This year's holiday shopping spree is expected to boost U.S. retail sales 5.5 percent compared to last year, according to The Conference Board.
The average American household will spend $450 on gifts this holiday season, up from $430 last year, according to a report issued by the Conference Board.
"This increase, in conjunction with household population growth, will lift the U.S. retail sales over the $45 billion mark -- a 5.5 percent increase over holiday sales last year," the report said.
Pacing the nation, New England households will spend an average of $722 on holiday gifts this year, the report said.
The lowest average spending levels will be in the Rocky Mountain region, about $360, according to the report.

"The anticipated rise in holiday spending is consistent with recent economic trends, marked by strong consumer confidence levels, moderate inflationary pressures and continuing wage gains," said Lynn Franco, associate director of the Consumer Research Center.
"While not all retailers will benefit equally, this Christmas has all the makings of a successful season."
The survey covered a nationally representative sample of 5,000 households and it was conducted in November for The Conference Board by NFO Inc.
* Slightly more than 30 percent of homes intend to spend $500 or more for Christmas gifts
* More than two out of every five households have set aside $200-$500 to spend on gifts
* Less than 30 percent of households are projected to spend less than $200 for holiday giving this year
